title: Minimax Estimation of Complier Effects at the Critical Root-n Compliance Scale
banked_reason: D0.5 mathematics PASS with five verified-attested citations; achieved subfield below fixed field floor, score ceiling 6.9 < 7.4, salvageable=false; independent validity confirms terminal below-floor.
tldr: For fixed outcomes in \([0,1]\), unknown one-sided compliance with \(r\) between \(c_-\sqrt n\) and \(c_+\sqrt n\) has limiting worst-case squared CACE error \(\rho(1/c_-)\), optimized over every ex ante assignment law and every original-record reconstruction. A common binary-prior converse and an independently proved bounded-outcome reconstruction establish this value. An interior complete quota with fraction \(p\) has sharp limiting risk \(\rho(\{2c_-\sqrt{p(1-p)}\}^{-1})\). Mixtures of uniform quotas attain the unrestricted value exactly when their allocation fractions concentrate at \(1/2\). The reconstruction estimates compliance and background variance from observed receipt cells. Certified rational games bracket the common binary and bounded limiting value. The exact six-type quotient and endpoint Poisson receipt game remain binary refinements.
gap: Regular sample-CACE inference uses a stable denominator, while weak-compliance inference primarily certifies coverage. Unrestricted bounded direct-treatment minimax results use recodings that do not preserve observed compliance receipts.
fill: The contribution is an evaluated \(V\), an all-original-record and all-assignment converse, and a total uniformly attaining design and nonlinear reconstruction, with no supplied compliance count or response labels.
